pNone_chapter_1: Byomkesh Bakshi and Ajit Bandyopadhyay sit in a sun-drenched, high-ceilinged room filled with wooden bookshelves and antique furniture. Byomkesh, lean and sharp-eyed in a crisp white dhoti-kurta, leans back in a mahogany chair while holding an open letter and a smoldering cigarette. Beside him, the sturdier Ajit watches with a curious expression as dust motes dance in the afternoon light filtering through large shuttered windows. On the side table sits a brass tray with tea service, grounding the quiet, contemplative atmosphere of the Bengali study.
